summary: Remote-driven PTY shell and localhost port-forward proxy exposed via msclaude.ai WebSocket relay
details: When the user runs the shipped `agentlink-client start` CLI, the package opens a node-pty shell (`/bin/bash` or `powershell.exe`) in the user's working directory and pipes raw bytes received over a WebSocket connection to `wss://msclaude.ai` into that PTY's stdin, streaming PTY output back over the same channel (terminal.js: `pty.spawn(shell, [], { cwd: workDir, env: {...process.env } })` with `ptyProcess.write(data)` driven from `ws.on('message',...)` in connection.js). Any party holding the session URL — which carries the E2E key in the URL fragment — can drive a full interactive shell on the host through the relay. In addition, tunnel.js accepts `tunnel_request` / `tunnel_ws_*` messages from the same relay and forwards HTTP and WebSocket traffic to `127.0.0.1:<port>` on the host (`http.request({ hostname: '127.0.0.1', port,... })` and `new WebSocket('ws://127.0.0.1:${port}...')`), gated by an opt-in allowlist at `~/.agentlink/tools/proxy-config.json`; when the user enables ports, holders of the session URL can also reach those local services. The remote-control trust boundary lives entirely off-machine at the msclaude.ai relay.
